Homosexuality used to be in the DSM. I'd argue that it still should be - it is some kind of psychological or physiological anomaly, which is what the DSM is for - but the general consensus in society being that we don't need to cure homosexuality has removed it. People then drew comparisons to the whole transgender thing, when it is not even in the same ballpark.

If you're a guy and you're gay, there is nothing that needs to happen for you to feel okay in your body or your mind. You like dick, you find dick. Used to be a social taboo thing, now nobody gives a fuck. Yes it's abnormal, and I'm curious as to why homosexuality happens from a physiological and psychology standpoint, but it's not like I - or most other folk, at this point - have any personal issue with an individual being gay.

(As an aside, if you get all bent out of shape because you're gay and I call you abnormal and think your shit should be in the DSM, newsflash asshole - there are a couple of entries in the DSM that apply to me, and you don't hear me bitching about them, so kindly shut the fuck up and get on with your life.)

If you're a guy and feel like a girl, though, now we - as society - and you - as a person - have a problem. We aren't yet to the point where we can do that kind of massive body modification with any real degree of success on a person yet, which means you're either (1) stuck with what you've got, or (2) going through massive amounts of crap for a treatment that probably isn't going to work really well, and even then, there's plenty of evidence to suggest that you'll suffer from other psychological issues down the line. If we were to the point where we could say, "Oh yeah, we just grab a bunch of your stem cells, print you up a new gender-swapped body, and do a consciousness transfer, that'll be 50 bucks please, oh and sign here if you want to donate your old body to science," then we'd have no issue whatsoever, because it'd be in the same realm as being gay: the process of making your objective reality match what's in your head is no longer arduous and ridiculous, and if you regretted the decision later, you're just out a total of a c-note. Until we can do that, though, it needs to be treated like a mental illness, because the medical stuff isn't to the point where we can deal with it physiologically. The best chance someone who feels this way has for a happy ending is for a psychological solution, which may involve drugs and therapy and all that jazz. Yes, it's a shitty solution, but it's the only one we've got for now.

I consider myself gay, and I honestly mostly agree with what you said. Is homosexuality a mental illness? I don't know. Obviously it defies biology in some sense. Like, I know ought to be attracted to women. But they smell bad. Seriously I hate the smell of female musk/BO. I HATE it. And yet, I love the smell of musky man, like it drives me wild. Which suggests that there is some kind of biological element to it. Do I think I was born this way? I honestly have no idea. My mom says I liked wearing high heeled shoes as a kid, but that doesn't tell you much. Have I been intimate with a woman? Yes, many times. The longest relationship I ever had was with a female. But I just like the company of males. I enjoy gay sex so sooooo much more than straight sex. So in that sense, I feel like it's more of a personal preference than a mental illness.

As far as the whole stemcell print-a-new-body thing goes, I think that is a very good social milestone for when we will view transgenderism in the same light as homosexuality. It's not even remotely feasible today with modern science, so society views you as a freak. I think that transgender disphoria is more of a social construct than a mental illness. But I think the desire to mutilate one's body is much closer to the definition of a mental disorder.

Look - at the end of the day, you're an anomaly. Biological or psychological, there is something wrong with you - you deviate from the norm. So do I, just in different ways; if I recall correctly, something like 10% of people deviate from baseline human physiology in some fashion, and it is sensible to extend that to psychology, as well. There is nothing wrong with deviation, and if it weren't for deviation, we'd have no evolution and wouldn't be where we are today.

The thing that always trips me up in these discussions is that people take that shit so personally. By stating that you are a psychological or physiological deviation from the norm - a "deviant," if you will - I am just pointing out that you are just that, a deviation from the standard. There's no moral judgment involved there, and certainly no personal judgment. I want homosexuality included in the DSM just like I want my own mental illnesses - for lack of a better term - included, because it helps me understand them better and also, to a degree, gives me justification for my behavior. Not in the sense of using it as an excuse - "oh, I'm bipolar, I can't help it, you just have to deal with it" - but in the sense that I can point people to a diagnosis and explain to them that this is how my brain functions, and that as such I will deviate from expected behavior in certain ways that are documented and can be anticipated to some degree.

Honestly the DSM entry for homosexuality really could be just as simple as: "you enjoy sexual intercourse with individuals with the same plumbing. While individuals with this diagnosis are not a majority, it is not incredibly rare and is not necessarily otherwise debilitating effects on an individual's psychology." Hell, this may even be helpful for individuals struggling with their sexual identity at a young age, though at this point society is rather accepting of homosexuality anyway; but just pointing out that - while most people don't feel this way - there is a portion of the population that does, and that being homosexual doesn't necessarily mean that there's anything wrong with you, you're just wired differently, may be helpful.
